---
title: "Infrastructure on Start + Void"
description: "Cutover packet for the native Infrastructure Worker: names, bindings, build, smoke checks and rollback."
updatedAt: "2026-11-09"
audience: developers
---

`apps/infrastructure` has native TanStack Start + Vite+ + Void source beside its Next build,
generated by the [start-bridge codemod](/build/devops/start-bridge-codemod). The Next
build and `vercel.json` are untouched, so the current deployment keeps serving until
the route is flipped. `vercel-production-infrastructure.yaml` still deploys the Next app.

## Worker

- Staging candidate: the staging Worker name (`workers_dev` off, `TUTURUUU_NOINDEX=1`). A production Worker (`tuturuuu-infrastructure`, `workers_dev` and `preview_urls` off, `TUTURUUU_NOINDEX=0`) is created by the cutover PR; nothing here attaches a route.
- Entry: `apps/infrastructure/cloudflare/worker.ts`; Wrangler config is emitted by `void` into `dist`.
- Host: `infrastructure.tuturuuu.com`. Root-only: `mountHosts` is empty and `unknownHost` is `reject`, so `tuturuuu.com/infrastructure` and any other host answer 404 before app code runs.
- Binding: `ASSETS` (static output, `run_worker_first`).
- Variables (names): `TUTURUUU_NOINDEX`, optional `INTERNAL_WEB_API_ORIGIN` (default `https://tuturuuu.com`).
- Secrets (names, set in the Worker, never in the repo): `NEXT_PUBLIC_SUPABASE_URL`, `NEXT_PUBLIC_SUPABASE_PUBLISHABLE_KEY`, `SUPABASE_SECRET_KEY`, `TUTURUUU_APP_COORDINATION_SECRET`, `TUTURUUU_AZURE_TENANT_ID`, `ENCRYPTION_MASTER_KEY`, `CRON_SECRET`, `OPS_HUB_GATEWAY_SECRET`, `OPS_HUB_WORKER_URL`, `CHAT_REALTIME_TOKEN_SECRET`, `AUTH_RECOVERY_HASH_SECRET`, `GITHUB_TOKEN`. Compare with the Vercel project environment list before the flip.
- Other names the source reads (verify each against the Vercel project list before the flip; set only the ones that project defines): `FIREBASE_PROJECT_ID`, `FIREBASE_CLIENT_EMAIL`, `FIREBASE_PRIVATE_KEY`, `MODAL_TOKEN_ID`, `MODAL_TOKEN_SECRET`, `EMAIL_UNSUBSCRIBE_SECRET`, `INVENTORY_SIMULATED_ORDER_SECRET`, `OPS_HUB_ALLOWED_USER_IDS`, `REQUIRED_MFA_POLICY_ENABLED`.
- Known gap: `vite.config.mts` aliases `playwright` to a stub that always fails, so only the Zalo web sync reports the browser as unavailable on Workers; every other route is unaffected. The Docker, blue-green, cron-control and stress-test panels read `PLATFORM_*` host paths and tokens that do not exist on Workers; they report unavailable there. Do not rerun the start-bridge codemod on this app without restoring the `playwright` alias in `vite.config.mts`.

## Build and qualification

```bash
bun install --frozen-lockfile --ignore-scripts
bun turbo:local run build --filter=@tuturuuu/infrastructure^... --concurrency=2
bun scripts/ci/generate-build-metadata.ts
bun run --cwd apps/infrastructure routes:check
bun run --cwd apps/infrastructure type-check:cloudflare
bun run --cwd apps/infrastructure build:cloudflare
CI=true CI_SOURCE_SHA=$(git rev-parse HEAD) bun run --cwd apps/infrastructure test:runtime
```

`infrastructure-cloudflare.yaml` runs the same steps in CI. `test:runtime` starts the emitted Worker in workerd
with synthetic secrets and no network egress: build identity, root host, apex rejection,
unknown paths, and the signed-out redirect through the app-owned
`cloudflare/auth-redirect.runtime.mjs` fixture (8 checks).

The app proxy admits anonymous `GET`/`HEAD /api/build-info` without an app-session
refresh, so deployment verification gets `200` instead of `401`.

## Smoke checks after the route is attached

```bash
curl -sI https://infrastructure.tuturuuu.com/api/build-info   # 200, JSON, no-store
curl -sI https://infrastructure.tuturuuu.com/                 # 307 to /login for a signed-out client
curl -sI https://infrastructure.tuturuuu.com/login            # renders, no 5xx
curl -sI https://tuturuuu.com/infrastructure        # 404 (root-only app)
```

Every page redirects signed-out users to login, so a signed-in check needs a test
session and belongs to the release owner. No smoke request may return `5xx`.

## Rollback

1. Before the flip, record the current production Vercel deployment id for the app (the repo
   does not store it) and the DNS records and TTLs for `infrastructure.tuturuuu.com` in the release record.
2. Roll back by detaching the Worker route or restoring the captured DNS records to the
   recorded deployment. `vercel-production-infrastructure.yaml` still deploys the Next app.
3. Rerun the smoke checks against the previous origin.

Rolling back touches no database rows and no migrations. Route, DNS and deployment
changes belong to the release owner.
